description: Team Still Out There is a solo dev unit out of Osogbo, Nigeria, using AI prototyping for the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge. We combine open NASA datasets with a sleek frontend to map space debris on the Moon and Mars, creating an interactive educational tool to inspire future space enthusiasts.
summary:
Still Out There is an interactive story-based website with modelling based off Three.js, and real NASA data that brings accurate information about 17 spacecrafts, historic and inaccurate, back into focus.

While space exploration is mainly about active missions and big wins, there are rovers, landers, probes and other spacecraft that remain silent and lost across the solar system. Designed for people ages 10-14, this website addresses the challenges of trying to make space history fun and important by letting each spacecraft tell it's own purpose and story, paired with the real science that made it possible, live telemetry, animations and different point of views the user can use to see the entire solar system.

By changing raw data and distances into an interactive experience for all, Still Out There makes it easier to visualize astronomy with human curiosity, an attempt to inspire the next generation to appreciate the engineering and space exploration that would otherwise be missing unless for these lost heros out there.
details:
Still Out There is an interactive browser-based 3D tour of the solar system that highlights the 17 historic, inactive and active, or abandoned spacecrafts from early lunar landings to deep spacecrafts like the Voyager. I built this using HTML, JavaScript and Three.js, which allows for 3D modelling with trajectories and starfields. Users can select different stops along their journey where each spacecraft tells its own story and has different data with a corresponding NASA link for each craft with a button to look back onto Earth and send a signal to see how fast it takes for it to reach Earth.

This project was designed in mind for people of young age with its fast paced and interaction, around the age of 10-14. By focusing on lost and forgotten spacecrafts, the project tries to honor the feats of human engineering and teaches kids that even failures can show the way to understanding our world.

For languages, i used HTML, CSS and JavaScript. I use Three.js for 3D modelling and different animations and Google Fonts for fonts of course. I use NASA mission pages, telemetry data and the NSSDCA. This is developed to run entirely on the web with 0 installation and downloads for users.

Most space projects focus on cool rockets or big wins made by active missions. Still Out There tries to take a different approach by trying to create a narrative, creative way to humanizing inactive and failed historic technologies with their own stories. By implementing 3D modelling such as craft trajectories, starts, and signal pulses and storytelling, it turns boring, raw data from random machines to an inspiration and fun approach to science.

In this project, I factored in age appropriate UX design to keep things simple for young viewers without making it too boring. I also factored in performance and accessibility so my program doesn't crash, and I also tried to keep things scientifically accurate and to add engagement into my website with cinematic animations while maintaining educational value.
